name: Dougie Cochrane
summary: Rated the best prospect in the crop even after knee tendinitis wiped out most of his top-age year. A 196cm athlete who has played forward, back and through the middle, and showed it in four SANFL League games late in the season, mostly in defence.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Cody Walker
summary: Carlton father-son midfielder: explosive, relentless and very consistent, with real stoppage craft and the engine to match (third in the national combine 2km). Ball use under pressure is the main thing to tidy up.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Arki Butler
summary: Flashy forward who can win a game on his own with goals and push into the midfield from stoppages. Captained Brighton Grammar to an APS flag. Four-quarter consistency is the knock.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Gus Teixeira
summary: Powerful midfielder who bursts out of contests and hurts teams going inside 50, then goes forward and kicks goals. All-Australian despite a foot injury delaying his start.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Ethan Drever
summary: Big-volume inside midfielder: 29 disposals, 6 tackles and a goal a game, Vic Country MVP, and an elite athlete for a 188cm mid (top five in the combine sprint and running jump). Foot skills under pressure are the work-on. A natural fantasy scorer profile.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Heath Mellody
summary: 2026 Larke Medallist and WA's standout: an elite user of the ball who links play and covers huge ground, built for transition footy off half-back or the wing.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Harry Van Hattum
summary: 205cm ruck with real speed and spring (top-six combine running jump) who also threatens forward; compared to Cooper Duff-Tytler. Quiet at the carnival, better in the back half of the Talent League. Rucks take time in fantasy.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Ethan Matthews
summary: GWS academy runner who grew from a wing and half-back into a damaging midfielder, with monster Talent League numbers (35 touches, 9 inside 50s, ~3 goals a game) and six VFL games. A foot stress reaction cut his carnival short.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Mitch Harris
summary: All-Australian full back: brave, competitive intercept marker who reads the play and holds up one-on-one. His kicking out of defence is the thing holding him back.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Caylen Murray
summary: Dynamic Queensland playmaker who carves teams up with speed and quick ball movement, marks strongly and kicks goals from range. Fourth in the combine 2km. Getting VFL exposure.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Wil Malady
summary: High-upside tall forward and genuine game-breaker: kicked five in Gippsland's Talent League premiership and was top three for both speed and agility at the combine. Low volume and consistency are the questions.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Leo Steed
summary: Hard-tackling, competitive midfielder-forward who held his own in 12 WAFL League games and made the All-Australian side. Scouts say he'd be top-five if he were taller.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Clancy Snell
summary: Fast-improving key defender, among the most complete talls in the crop: intercepts and reads the play well, rarely fumbles and is composed enough to start attacks. Part of Gippsland's premiership.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Sam Gayfer
improvements: Holding overhead marks on the lead
summary: Physical key forward who kicked 28 goals in 12 games, tackles hard and topped both combine jumps. Needs to stick more marks on the lead; some clubs see him as a defender.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Lochie Burrows
summary: Tough, athletic utility who has played midfield and defence for Sandringham. Versatile and competitive, and seen as a chance to push into the top 20.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Tyson Bradley
summary: Unflappable key defender, Vic Metro MVP and Talent League Team of the Year captain. Wins his one-on-ones, positions superbly and distributes calmly. Not quick.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Toby Krasna
summary: Crafty, agile wingman with elite running patterns and slick skills on both feet; 21 touches a game before a hamstring injury. Light frame for now.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Jackson Phillips
summary: Stylish big improver who can win it at stoppages or run on the outside, kicks well off both feet and chips in with a goal a game. Also got VFL exposure.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: George Dimer
summary: Smart, clean small forward with excellent kicking inside 50 and top-three agility at the combine. A specialist whose size is the obvious limit.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Harvie Cooke
summary: Morrish Medallist (Talent League best and fairest) who rose from bottom-age regular to genuine prospect: 25 disposals, 6 clearances and 5 tackles a game, then All-Australian. Top five in the combine 2km and agility. Strong fantasy-style output.

source.title: Rock and Cooke earn Talent League best and fairests

name: Khaled El Souki
summary: Western Bulldogs academy small forward who led the Talent League goalkicking (40 in 12) and finds the goals from every angle, while still getting 19 touches. An ankle injury limited his carnival.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Noah Williams
improvements: Needs to become a full-time midfielder
summary: Tough, skilled leader who tackles hard and hurts teams with speed and kicking off a wing or half-back. Still has to nail down a midfield role and recapture his best form.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Jack Pickett
summary: Strong-marking key forward who kicked 31 goals in eight games as a bottom-ager, but a knee injury wiped out most of his draft year. A pure upside play.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Jake Eime
summary: Fast, attacking rebounder who plays at full speed and averaged 22 touches in the Talent League plus two SANFL games. Exciting with the ball; his high tempo can invite pressure.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Albert MacGowan
summary: All-Australian wingman and Talent League Team of the Year pick who ran the fastest 2km at the national combine. A pure running wing; his inside game is the question.

source.title: Top 10s: 2026 National AFL Draft Combine

name: George Gale
summary: Tall All-Australian wingman with a big engine who is growing into an inside ball winner and averaged 19 touches in three WAFL League games. Not quick.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Billy Wigmore
improvements: Hesitant with ball in hand at times
summary: Intercept-marking defender who reads the play early and backs himself in the air; took 10 marks against Oakleigh in the wildcard round. Needs more confidence with the ball and is undersized for a key back.

source.title: Scouting Notes: Oakleigh charges into finals with Wildcard win

name: Archie Elliott
summary: Plays like a tall forward in a 182cm frame: leads up, marks reliably and follows up hard at ground level. Can be beaten in the air by bigger defenders.

source.title: Scouting Notes: Stingrays kick away late in Rebels raid

name: Kodah Edwards
summary: Competitive leader who explodes out of congestion and kicks goals when forward; held his own in five SANFL League games. Ball use can be scrappy.

source.title: AFL Draft Power Rankings: August 2026 Top 50

name: Keenan Boi
summary: Hawthorn academy small forward who pushed into the midfield in Gippsland's premiership, bringing speed, strong tackling and low, drilling kicks. His goal sense comes and goes.

source.title: Scouting Notes: 2026 Talent League Grand Final
